text: dsh-voice-mode-desktop 是面向 DSH 0.2 桌面会话的语音插件，在对话输入区加入麦克风按钮、状态栏和语音覆盖层，并提供侧边栏设置页。它把语音识别结果流式写入草稿，可按住说话或持续聆听，并可在静音后自动发送；AI 回复会逐句合成为语音并显示字幕，用户说话时可打断朗读。设置页可调整输入方式、语速、音色、识别与朗读引擎及字幕。默认 Edge 朗读会把待合成文本发送给微软语音服务；本地引擎和识别模型需要下载模型文件。

dsh-voice-mode-desktop adds voice input and spoken replies to DSH desktop chats. Recognition streams into an editable draft; replies are read aloud sentence by sentence with captions and can be interrupted by speaking. Default Edge read-aloud sends text to Microsoft's speech service.
我想直接对着电脑说话，让识别结果先进入可编辑的聊天草稿。
能不能把 DSH 的回复逐句读出来，还能同步显示字幕？
I want hands-free voice input for a desktop chat, with recognized speech appearing in the draft.
dsh-voice-mode-desktop 的功能「语音朗读与字幕」：将回复逐句合成为语音并显示字幕；用户再次说话时可中断当前朗读。
dsh-voice-mode-desktop 的功能「语音输入」：从对话输入区的麦克风入口进入语音模式，将识别内容写入草稿，并支持按住说话或持续聆听。
dsh-voice-mode-desktop 使用 Edge 朗读引擎时，会把待朗读文本发送到 speech.platform.bing.com 合成音频；切换本地朗读引擎可避免这项云端合成。

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · dsh-voice-mode-desktop：English | [中文](./README.zh.md)

Full-duplex voice mode for **DeepSeek Harness 0.2 (desktop)**: speak and the words stream into the draft, pause and the message sends, the reply is read sentence by sentence, and speaking again interrupts the read-aloud. Ships an in-app settings page for reading speed, input mode and captions.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · dsh-voice-mode-desktop：This is an adapted fork of [`dsh-voice-mode`](https://github.com/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode) 0.7.15 (which in turn derives from [`haoku123/dsh-voice`](https://github.com/haoku123/dsh-voice)). Both are MIT licensed; see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · dsh-voice-mode-desktop：**What this fork is:** the compatibility adaptation that makes that plugin run on DSH 0.2 desktop — it adapts the client API the plugin depends on, adds an in-app settings page, and replaces the cloud read-aloud dependency with a small client kept inside this repository. The recognition, barge-in and local-TTS engines are upstream work, unchanged.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · What it does：- **Voice in**: press-and-hold or continuous listening, streaming recognition into an editable draft, silence-based auto-send.
- **Voice out**: sentence-by-sentence read-aloud (Edge cloud TTS by default; local VITS / Kokoro optional), live captions.
- **Full duplex**: speaking while the reply is read stops playback and cancels the running turn.
- **Settings page**: reading speed (0.5–2.0), input mode (hold / continuous), caption show-hide, and a one-click audio self-test. Reachable from the sidebar **Plugins** page as the item **语音模式 / Voice mode**. The self-test deliberately separates synthesis from playback, so a silent reply can be traced to the engine or to the audio output instead of being guessed at.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · One conversation, end to end：1. Hold the shortcut and speak; recognition streams into an editable draft.
2. Release to submit; the agent starts replying.
3. Replies are synthesized sentence by sentence while captions follow along.
4. Speaking again during playback interrupts it immediately and starts the next turn.
5. One action decides everything: releasing is what tells it you are done talking.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · How to use it: hold to speak：Day to day this plugin is meant to be used **hold-to-speak**: hold the shortcut, say one sentence, release. In the voice session pick "hold" as the recording mode and "manual" as the barge-in mode.
section: How to use it: hold to speak

text: @nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · How to use it: hold to speak：**Full duplex (always listening + auto barge-in) is not the recommended everyday mode, and it has no regression coverage.** The reason is practical: it hands the timing to the model. It may start acting before you finish, or keep listening after you are done, and you lose control over when it stops and when it acts. Hold-to-speak keeps both decisions with you: release means the sentence is finished, and only then may it act.
section: How to use it: hold to speak

text:
@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · How to use it: hold to speak：- Want predictable control: hold-to-speak + manual barge-in (recommended).
- Trying full duplex: fine, but treat it as experimental. If it talks over you or fails to stop, switch back to hold-to-speak before blaming the plugin.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Test environment：All speed and resource numbers below come from this machine, not from synthetic or borrowed figures:

- CPU: Intel Core i5-14490F
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (8 GB VRAM)
- RAM: 32 GB
- OS: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

Different hardware scales the numbers; VRAM use depends on whether the GPU tier is loaded.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Recognition engines (three tiers)：| Tier | Model | Runs on | Speed | Resources | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU preferred | Nano bf16 | GPU | ~0.4 s/sentence | ~6-9 s first load, ~1.9 GB VRAM resident | Most accurate, default |
| CPU only | Nano int8 | CPU | ~0.9 s/sentence | No VRAM, no Python needed | Slightly slower but steady |
| SenseVoice only | SenseVoice int8 | CPU | Fast | Lightest | Weaker on English terms |

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Recognition engines (three tiers)：Switching takes effect immediately and is written to disk, so it survives a restart. The settings page shows the current tier, GPU layer status and last recognition latency.

Accuracy (observed on the same Chinese test corpus; no standard WER benchmark was run):

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Read-aloud engines：| Engine | Where | Traits | Speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edge | Cloud | Many voices, needs network | Network-dependent |
| ZipVoice | Local GPU | Voice cloning, natural mixed Chinese/English | ~0.6 s/sentence, up to 2x playback with time-domain splicing |
| VITS | Local CPU | Lightweight offline | Slower than GPU options |
| Kokoro | Local | Lightweight fallback | Fast, but mispronounces English words |
@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Read-aloud engines：The first synthesis after switching engines takes a few seconds to load the model; afterwards it runs per sentence.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Differences from upstream `dsh-voice-mode` 0.7.15：| Area | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Client half | `inject` no longer declares `settingsScope`; the access is wrapped in `try`/`catch` | `settingsScope` was removed from the DSH client API; the host treats "one entry did not activate" as fatal and the desktop app drops into recovery |
| Settings schema | `rate` and `mode` are marked `volatile`, and volatile values are unwrapped at every read site | DSH 0.2 renders only `volatile` fields in plugin forms; a wrapped value passed to the TTS engine makes synthesis fail silently |
| Settings UI | New in-app page (sidebar Plugins → 语音模式) plus host endpoint `POST /voice-mode/settings`; laid out like the host's own settings pages and themed with host design tokens (`--dsw-alias-*`) | The upstream settings card depends on the removed client API, and the host page that renders plugin config forms is not mounted in the desktop deployment |
| Captions | Added a show/hide switch; caption max width capped (420 px default tier) | Captions are optional; the previous default could span most of the window |
| Status bar | Width is content-sized, centered

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Differences from upstream `dsh-voice-mode` 0.7.15：Everything else — recognition, TTS engines, barge-in, wake word, backchannel yield, model pinning — is upstream code, unchanged.
@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Change scope：Baseline: `dsh-voice-mode@0.7.15` as published on npm (itself derived from `haoku123/dsh-voice`). Files touched by this fork:

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Change scope：| File | Nature of change |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | host half: `volatile` fields in the settings schema, `POST /voice-mode/settings`, one diagnostic log line; the Edge engine now calls the in-repo client instead of `msedge-tts` |
| `lib/client.js` | client half: `inject` list, `settingsScope` guard, the settings page, caption show/hide and width, status-bar width |
| `lib/edge-tts.js` | new in this fork |
| `cordis.patch.yml`, `package.json` | mount point and packaging metadata (renamed package, no install scripts) |
| `scripts/verify-compat.mjs`, `scripts/check-tts.mjs` | new in this fork |

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Change scope：`lib/sense-worker.mjs` and `lib/tts-vits-worker.cjs` are upstream files, byte-identical. The upstream project keeps its own git history, tests and build pipeline; this fork is a compatibility adaptation, not a rewrite.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Install：The plugin is a DSH bundle. In a profile:

```bash
@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · from the npm registry …：dsh plugin add @nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop
@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · … or from a local checkout：dsh plugin add link:/path/to/dsh-voice-mode-desktop

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · dependency: "@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop": "git+https://github.com/NutshellLee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop.git"：```

Then enable it in the profile manifest (`dsh.profile.bundles`) and, optionally, override defaults in the profile patch:

```yaml
- id: voice-mode
  config:
    enabled: true
    voice: zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural
    rate: 1.1
    mode: hold          # hold = push to talk, toggle = continuous listening
    ttsEngine: edge     # edge | vits | kokoro
    bargeInMode: detect
    silenceMs: 1500
    autoSend: true
    spokenFormat: true
```

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · dependency: "@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop": "git+https://github.com/NutshellLee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop.git"：Restart the app after the first install, then open **Plugins → 语音模式** to adjust settings, or press `Ctrl+Shift+V` inside a conversation.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Cloud read-aloud status：The Edge engine talks to Microsoft's read-aloud endpoint directly from `lib/edge-tts.js` (WebSocket handshake, SSML request, MP3 frames). No third-party TTS wrapper is involved, so installation needs no install script and no dependency patching. To check the path on your machine:

```bash
node scripts/check-tts.mjs
```

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Cloud read-aloud status：The read-aloud connection picks up a proxy automatically: `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` first, otherwise the Windows system proxy from Settings (the `ProxyServer` value under `Internet Settings`). Microsoft is picky about the source IP — on some networks a direct connection is answered with 403 while going through a proxy works, and `ws` ignores the system proxy by default, so the client has to do this itself. To force a direct connection, set `NO_PROXY` to `speech.platform.bing.com`.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Verify：```bash
node scripts/verify-compat.mjs [path-to-dsh-app]
```

Checks the contract this fork depends on: the DSH app is present, all nine client inject targets exist, the host no longer serves `settingsScope`, the plugin's client half declares no missing service, and `rate`/`mode` project as live-editable fields. Exit code 0 means all checks passed.
@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Models：No model files are bundled. The plugin downloads what it needs the first time that capability is used, then reuses the local copy.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Models：| Capability | Downloaded when | Source repository |
|---|---|---|
| Streaming recognition (default) | first voice input | `csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-streaming-zipformer-zh-int8-2025-06-30` (encoder / decoder / joiner / tokens) |
| Voice activity detection | first voice input | Silero VAD (`silero_vad.onnx`) |
| SenseVoice recognition (`senseVoice: true`) | first voice input | SenseVoice int8 (`model.int8.onnx` + tokens) |
| Local VITS read-aloud (`ttsEngine: vits`) | first read-aloud with that engine | `csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-vits-zh-ll` |
| Local Kokoro read-aloud (`ttsEngine: kokoro`) | first read-aloud with that engine | Kokoro int8 model set |

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Models：- **Hosts**: `huggingface.co` first, `hf-mirror.com` as fallback. Only those two (plus `hf.co`) are accepted unless `allowCustomHost: true` is set in the profile patch. Set `modelHost` to pin a mirror.
- **Cache directory**: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-voice-mode\models` on Windows, `~/.cache/dsh-voice-mode/models` elsewhere.
- **Integrity**: every file is checked against a pinned SHA-256 before use; partial downloads are written next to the target and only renamed once they verify.
- **Progress**: download and load progress is reported in the voice status bar; failures are surfaced in the chat rather than silently ignored.
- **Offline**: recognition needs the model files (and `ttsEngine: edge` needs network on every read-aloud). To run fully offline, pre-populate the cache directory and use `vits` / `kokoro`.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Restart-plugin integration：This plugin can pair with [`dsh-agent-restart`](https://github.com/NutshellLee/dsh-agent-restart). When the agent restarts the app itself, that plugin records whether voice mode was on and writes a handover file after restart; this plugin reads it on startup, restores voice mode automatically (hold and speak), and deletes the file after a confirmed resume.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Restart-plugin integration：It only applies to agent-initiated restarts; closing and reopening the app by hand does not auto-restore. Without the restart plugin, this plugin works on its own.

@nutshelllee/dsh-voice-mode-desktop README · Known limitations：- **Compiled artifacts**: `lib/` is upstream's built output with this fork's edits applied, not regenerated from source. Read the diff against `dsh-voice-mode@0.7.15` rather than expecting readable source.
- **Cloud TTS by default**: `ttsEngine: edge` sends the spoken text to Microsoft. Use `vits` or `kokoro` for fully local synthesis.
- **Barge-in on speakers** depends on the browser's echo cancellation; on Windows, hold-to-talk or headphones give the most reliable interruption.
- **Settings persistence** covers `rate` and `mode` (the two `volatile` fields). Other options are read from the profile patch at startup.
- **Diagnostics write to a local log**: to pin down "an entire utterance went missing", the plugin writes every finalised segment (up to 400 characters) plus a set of pipeline events into DSH's application log (`desktop-next.log`). The log stays on the machine and the diagnostics endpoint listens on loopback only (`POST /voice-mode/diag`, same-origin checked); its content, however, is your own dictated text — clear the log periodically, and avoid installing this on a shared account.
